question.problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

gives the following expressions for ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =-{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} & =-2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

By solving the first equation for ${x}_{1}$ and substituting it into the second equation, we obtain the following expressions for ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-{y}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} & =-2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =(-{y}_{1})^{2}-6(-{y}_{1})(-2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})+(-2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}-12{y}_{1}^{2}+6{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+4{y}_{1}^{2}-4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & =-7{y}_{1}^{2}+2{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
